Q: Different outputs for the same line in C when another line is commented A:

The constant expression 5/4 has type int since both operands have that type. You then pass the result of this expression to printf with a %f format specifier which expects a double. Using the wrong format specifier in a printf call triggers undefined behavior in your code.

Q: Why are MCPs needed at all? A:

For me MCP is the tooling allowing to provide concrete, deterministic tools to AI models.

So for instance, if you prompt LLM "give me library members", for LLM it would be meaningless or it would cause it to hallucinate about some imaginary library.

However, you can provide LLM some MCP server called "The Library Management" with tools such as "List all members".

In such situation, LLM would first look for any library resources it has at hand, so it would find our registered MCP server "The Library Management" and pick that to answer our prompt about the library.

Then this answer would not be hallucination, rather answer based on very deterministic information.

Q: Firefox sync API - does it exist? A:

https://docs.services.mozilla.com/sync/ looks comprehensive enough and I think it's up to date (the last commit on the repo is 8 days old). A Python client is available on GitHub: https://github.com/mozilla-services/syncclient.

There's also a Sync to Kinto bridge, to use the Kinto interface to access the Sync data: https://github.com/mozilla-services/syncto

Q: What is an MCP server, and what core concepts should an entry-level developer understand? A:

I think official docs at modelcontextprotocol.io are more than enough to understand MCP. I have read all the resources there and it helped me to understand core concepts.

Plus, it has also "how-to" tutorials with SDKs for various programming languages.

As I am C# dev, I also found useful dedicated posts from C# community about MCPs useful:

  • Build a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in C#

Q: I'm working on implementing MCP servers in vscode. Which IDE and MCP is currently used more in industry right now? A:

Also, usage of MCP servers depends on who you would ask.

For example, graphic designers might rely heavily on MCP servers integrating Figma into LLMs.

However, this would not be as much useful for project managers, who would prefer more MCP servers integrating JIRA (or other project management system) into LLMs.

For developers, different MCP servers might be more useful.
